approach: Test-side generalisation in crates/athena-cap-study/src/rules.rs: replace the firstmate-only constants with `check_study(dir, pin_env, mount) -> Outcome` (`route` plus `problems`) and `check_studies(root, pin_env, mount)`. The kept test reads ATHENA_PIN_URL and ATHENA_PIN_SHA from the environment and passes them as arguments. Conventions run for every studies/*/ directory. Full validation runs only when the pin's URL and SHA equal the env pair and a mount exists. A same-URL, different-SHA pin fails naming the study id. A `synthetic_tree` rebuilt from a study's own citations lets temp-copy tests drive the matching branch in any checkout. The placeholder convention (UNRESOLVED, 'not examined') now runs on the parsed JSON values of each study file, skipping only `quote` strings inside a `sources` array, and names the owner id. `Study::admit` in lib.rs refuses a change spanning two studies/<id>/ directories and any path outside one study directory and CHANGELOG.md. The study producer prompt states the conventions and is rewritten within about 72 bytes of net growth, so the largest producer set stays at the recorded 1043 and docs/system-facts.md is not touched. If the set would grow past 1043, the producer tightens wording and never edits the facts file. xtask/tests/policy.rs gets `boundary_scan_file(path, text)`: it blanks only claim-source `quote` literals in `studies/<id>/claims.json`, found with a regex and decoded with serde_json, before word matching. Machine-path fragments always match on the raw text. Planted terms are split strings joined at run time.

decisions.choice: Pass the pin env pair and the mount path to `check_study` as arguments; only the kept test calls `std::env::var`.
decisions.reason: The workspace sets `unsafe_code = "deny"` (Cargo.toml line 59), so tests cannot call `set_var`. Arguments let temp-copy tests exercise every pin case in parallel without touching process state.

rejected.option: Tests set ATHENA_PIN_* with set_var
rejected.why: Needs unsafe in edition 2024 and races with parallel tests.

rejected.option: Run a child `cargo test` with env set
rejected.why: Slow, and the verifier may run only whole simple cargo commands.

decisions.choice: `check_study` returns `Outcome { route, problems }`. Tests drive the matching branch on temp copies using the study's own URL and SHA plus a `synthetic_tree` mount: (i) a validation.json with one rule result flipped gives a problem naming the study id and 'validation.json' with route FullyValidated; (ii) a changed claim quote gives a `quote-mismatch` problem naming the claim id, while the same edit with env unset gives route ConventionsOnly and no problems.
decisions.reason: Without these, a matching branch that returned early would pass every test. The tree for (i) and (ii) is built from the untouched study before the copy is edited, so it holds the original quote.

rejected.option: Rely on the mounted command alone
rejected.why: This job's verifier has no pinned-source/ and no code in the snapshot sets ATHENA_PIN_*.

rejected.option: Detect the route by capturing printed output
rejected.why: Fragile. A returned value is asserted directly.

decisions.choice: Reuse the existing `wrong_sha` rule (rules.rs:264-289) with a `NoTree` GitLookup for the source-SHA-differs-from-pin check; the offending id is the owner id the rule reports.
decisions.reason: `wrong_sha` only compares strings and never calls git for file sources, so it works with no tree and avoids a second comparison that could drift.

rejected.option: Re-implement the SHA comparison in the test
rejected.why: Duplicates logic that can drift from the rule.

decisions.choice: Put the convention checks in the `#[cfg(test)]` module of rules.rs, as the kept test is today; `RULES` (18 rules) is unchanged.
decisions.reason: The request names the kept test in rules.rs. New rules would change firstmate's validation.json, which may not change.

rejected.option: Add new entries to `RULES`
rejected.why: Would change firstmate's validation.json; nothing under studies/firstmate-work-handling/ may change.

decisions.choice: Finding 2 (critic): the placeholder convention runs on parsed values, not raw file text. `placeholders(dir)` reads each of pin.json, claims.json, rationales.json, model.json, findings.json and validation.json as `serde_json::Value`, and walks every string. The one exemption is the `quote` key of an object that is an element of a `sources` array. 'UNRESOLVED' is matched case-sensitively and 'not examined' case-insensitively (keeping rules.rs:1590-1591 semantics, so 'left unresolved' prose passes). The message starts with the nearest enclosing object's `id` string, or the study id (the directory name) when there is none. A test shows a claim source quote and a rationale source quote containing 'UNRESOLVED' and 'Not Examined' pass, while the same words in claim text, a card's `authors_say` and a finding detail fail naming the claim, card and finding ids.
decisions.reason: Every study must keep quotes verbatim (quote_mismatch, rules.rs:339-365). A studied system's source can contain these words, and a raw-text scan would make it impossible to pass: editing the quote would trip quote-mismatch. The request's item (4) already treats claim quotes as studied-source text. Walking parsed values also gives an owner id and avoids matching JSON keys or escapes. `authors_say` stays checked, because the request names only source quotes.

rejected.option: Keep the raw-text scan of each file
rejected.why: Fails any study whose quoted source uses these words (the critic's finding).

rejected.option: Case-insensitive match on UNRESOLVED
rejected.why: Flags the ordinary word 'unresolved' in prose.

rejected.option: Exempt every string in claims.json
rejected.why: Would hide placeholders in claim text, which is what the convention guards.

decisions.choice: With no mount, env unset, or env naming another URL, check conventions only. With env naming the pin's URL and SHA but no mount, conventions only. With env naming the pin's URL and a different SHA, fail naming the study id and both SHAs, whether or not a mount exists.
decisions.reason: This is the request's rule. A mismatch is a fault in pin.json or in the pinning, never a reason to validate quietly against the wrong tree. crates/athena-core/src/run/pin.rs `study_pin` (lines 82-133) lets several studies share one URL and picks one by study id, while the env pair carries no study id, so a job on study B makes study A (same URL, other SHA) fail. This goes in the CHANGELOG entry and in a User question.

rejected.option: Validate any mounted tree against every study
rejected.why: A second study would fail its own quote checks against firstmate's tree.

rejected.option: Compare only the study the pinning step picked
rejected.why: ATHENA_PIN_* has no study id and no code in the snapshot sets the pair.

rejected.option: Skip a same-URL different-SHA study silently
rejected.why: Criterion 2 requires a failure naming the id.

decisions.choice: The pinning change is a named precondition. The kept test prints a greppable line when `../../pinned-source` is a directory but no study matched the env pair: `WARNING: mounted tree present but no study matched ATHENA_PIN_*; tree validation did not run`. A pure `degradation_warning(routes, mount_present) -> Option<String>` is unit-tested for four inputs. The CHANGELOG says that with ATHENA_PIN_* unset the kept test checks conventions only, so the verifier prompt's 'code already ran the study's validation rules' holds only once the pinning change sets the pair.
decisions.reason: Today the kept test validates whenever pinned-source/ exists (rules.rs:1444). A grep of *.rs, *.md and *.toml for ATHENA_PIN finds nothing, so the loss would otherwise be silent. The test cannot fail on it: the accepted reading says unset means conventions only.

rejected.option: Fail the kept test when a mount exists but no env pair is set
rejected.why: Contradicts the accepted reading and criterion 1.

rejected.option: Fall back to validating every study against any mounted tree
rejected.why: A second study would fail against the wrong tree.

decisions.choice: Admission: collect `studies/<id>/...` ids over all non-build-output paths. More than one id gives one `study-one-directory` violation naming the ids. Every path that is not build output, not exactly `CHANGELOG.md` at the root and not under `studies/<id>/` gives a `study-outside-directory` violation. Paths with `.`, `..` or empty segments, and a bare `studies/<name>` file, count as outside. Build-output paths keep their single `build-output` violation.
decisions.reason: Matches the brief. The existing `build_output_is_refused` (lib.rs:187) still sees exactly one violation.

rejected.option: Also flag build output as outside the directory
rejected.why: Gives two violations for one path and breaks the existing test.

rejected.option: Allow files directly under studies/
rejected.why: They belong to no study id.

decisions.choice: Finding 3 (critic): the boundary exemption finds quote literals with a regex, `"quote"\s*:\s*"(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*"`, over the raw text of `studies/<id>/claims.json` (exactly one id segment). It decodes the captured literal with `serde_json::from_str::<String>` and blanks it (to `"quote": ""`, same line count) only when the decoded string equals a `sources[].quote` collected from the parsed claims. If the file does not parse as claims, nothing is exempt. Words are matched on the blanked text and machine-path fragments on the raw text. `boundary_scan` stays unchanged so `the_admission_scan_finds_what_the_policy_scan_finds` compares like with like. A test uses hand-written JSON whose quote has escaped characters (a `\/`, a `\"` and a `é`) around a planted split-string word and expects no hit.
decisions.reason: Comparing decoded values makes the match independent of how the file escapes a string. If decoding fails or the value is not a claim quote, nothing is blanked and the scan over-reports, which is the safe direction. xtask already has serde_json as a dependency and regex as a dev-dependency.

rejected.option: Replace the text `"quote": <literal>` using literals in the collected set (previous plan)
rejected.why: Misses when the file's escaping differs from a re-serialized value.

rejected.option: Skip all of claims.json, or all of studies/
rejected.why: Would hide a claim's own prose and the rest of the study.

rejected.option: Exempt rationale-card quotes too
rejected.why: The request names the claims' quote fields. Raised as a User question.

decisions.choice: Finding 1 (athena): docs/system-facts.md is removed from the files list and nothing edits it. The study prompt is rewritten as a net-small edit. The recorded largest producer set is 1043 and the study set is 1018 (1200 minus the 182 headroom in criterion 5), so the prompt may grow by at most 25 tokens (about 72 bytes net over the current 1019). The producer runs `cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets`. If `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` reports a larger producer value, the producer shortens the prompt wording and runs it again. The order of cuts is: first the one-directory sentence, which admission enforces with a violation naming the allowed set; then the wording of existing bullets. The three conventions (tags, no placeholders with quotes exempt, 'none' never checked by code) and every existing rule stay.
decisions.reason: The reading's deliverables do not include the facts file, and the facts file says to update the line, never the budget. Staying inside the recorded maximum needs no facts edit, and the 1200 budget is untouched.

rejected.option: Update the producer budget line in docs/system-facts.md when the prompt grows
rejected.why: Not a listed deliverable; widens scope (the finding).

rejected.option: Raise the producer budget
rejected.why: The facts file forbids it.

rejected.option: Edit boundary.rs to tell study producers about the quote exception
rejected.why: Shared by every capability's brief and not a deliverable.

decisions.choice: `synthetic_tree(&Loaded) -> TempDir` builds each cited file as a vector of lines sized to the highest `end_line` cited for that path, appends each quote at its `start_line` (joining quotes that share a start line with one space), and writes the lines joined by newline. The tests first require `bad_citation` and `quote_mismatch` to report nothing on this tree.
decisions.reason: A one-quote-per-line layout collides on firstmate's data (docs/configuration.md 357-357 and 1088-1088, AGENTS.md 234-234, docs/agent-control.md 131-131, bin/fm-project-capacity-lib.sh 49-49, bin/fm-spawn.sh 3165-3165). `cited_lines` (rules.rs:292-299) joins the lines of the range and needs only `end <= lines.len()`, and `quote_mismatch` (339-365) checks a substring. The tree proves the route and the recorded equality, not that the real tree holds the quotes.

rejected.option: One quote per line, panic on collision
rejected.why: Panics on firstmate's real data.

rejected.option: Place colliding quotes on neighbouring lines
rejected.why: A single-line range cites exactly one line.

files.purpose: Replace the firstmate-only test section (from about line 1395) with `NoTree`, `Loaded::read(dir)`, `conventions` (including the parsed-value placeholder walk that skips `sources[].quote`), `check_study` returning `Outcome { route, problems }`, `check_studies`, `degradation_warning`, `synthetic_tree`, the kept test over every studies/*/, and the temp-copy fault tests. Non-test code is unchanged.

`admit()` also refuses a change spanning more than one studies/<id>/ and any path outside one study directory and CHANGELOG.md (build output keeps its own violation); add `study_dir_of` and unit tests.

State the conventions (enforcement tags, no placeholders with quotes exempt and verbatim, a 'none' guard never checked by code) within about 72 bytes of net growth by tightening existing wording. Keep every existing rule.
Split word and fragment scanning, add `boundary_scan_file` with the regex-found, decoded claim-quote exemption, use it in the tree scan, and add tests that plant split-string terms.

One entry under [Unreleased] / Changed describing per-study validation, the prompt conventions, the placeholder check skipping source quotes, the admission rule, the boundary exemption, the pinning precondition and degradation, and the several-studies-of-one-URL note.
Add `tempfile.workspace = true` to [dev-dependencies] for the temp-copy tests.
Add "tempfile" to the athena-cap-study dependency list so `--locked` passes.

steps: rules.rs test module: remove `STUDY_SHA`, `study_dir()`, the firstmate-only `mounted_tree()` and the fixed `STUDY_FILES` list (derive the file list from `studies/<dir>/`). Add `NoTree` (a GitLookup answering None/false), generalise `MountedTree::new(sha, root)`, and add `Loaded::read(dir) -> Result<Loaded, String>` (pin, claims, rationales, model, findings, validation) with `violations(git, rule)` and `validate(git)`. Before writing, grep firstmate's claims.json for escaped newlines in quotes and for source kinds other than file, and report what is found.

rules.rs: add `conventions(dir, loaded) -> Vec<String>`. It checks: pin.sha is 40-hex; `wrong_sha` (via `NoTree`) reports no owner; every claim text starts '[mechanism] ' or '[prose-only] '; every transition with guard 'none' has `guard_evaluated_by != Code` and empty `guard_counters`; pin.study_id and validation.study_id equal the directory name; each file source has a non-blank quote; and the placeholder walk (finding 2). The walk reads each study file as `serde_json::Value`, visits every string value, and skips only the `quote` key of an object that is an element of a `sources` array. 'UNRESOLVED' is matched case-sensitively and 'not examined' case-insensitively. The owner is the nearest enclosing object's `id` string, else the study id. Every message starts with the offending id.

rules.rs: add `enum Route { FullyValidated, ConventionsOnly }`, `struct Outcome { route, problems }` (derive Debug), `check_study(dir, pin_env: Option<(&str,&str)>, mount: Option<&Path>) -> Outcome` and `check_studies(root, pin_env, mount) -> Vec<(String, Outcome)>` (sorted directories, fails if none). Conventions always run. If the env url equals pin.repository_url and the sha differs, add a problem naming the study id and both SHAs (route ConventionsOnly). If url and sha are equal and a mount exists, run `validate()` with `MountedTree`, report each failing rule with its offending ids, report a problem naming the study id and 'validation.json' when `computed != validation.json`, and set route FullyValidated. Add `degradation_warning(routes, mount_present) -> Option<String>`, returning the warning line when a mount is present and no route is FullyValidated. The kept test `every_study_follows_the_conventions_and_the_matching_one_validates` reads the two env vars (non-empty), uses `../../pinned-source` if it is a directory, calls `check_studies` on `../../studies`, prints per study 'fully validated' or 'conventions only' plus the warning if any, and asserts no problems.

rules.rs: add `synthetic_tree(&Loaded) -> TempDir`: for every path cited by a file source, a vector of lines sized to the highest end_line cited for that path (blank by default). Append each quote at its start_line, joining quotes that share a line with one space, and write the lines joined by newline. Add tests: (a) `the_study_matching_the_pin_validates_against_a_tree_rebuilt_from_its_citations`: assert `bad_citation` and `quote_mismatch` report nothing on the tree, then route == FullyValidated, no problems, and `validate()` equals validation.json. (b) `a_matching_pin_runs_validation_and_reports_a_tampered_record_or_quote`: build the tree from the untouched study, copy the study to a TempDir, then in separate copies flip one rule result in validation.json (expect route FullyValidated and a problem containing the study id and 'validation.json') and change one claim quote (expect a problem containing the claim id and 'quote-mismatch'); the same quote edit with env unset gives ConventionsOnly and no problems. (c) `a_study_that_breaks_a_convention_or_its_pin_fails_naming_the_id`: four faults (untagged claim, none-guard checked by code, source SHA differing from the pin, same-URL different-SHA pin with a temp mount), plus a control. (d) `the_word_unresolved_in_prose_is_not_a_placeholder`: 'left unresolved' passes, 'UNRESOLVED' in claim text fails naming the claim id, 'Not Examined' in a finding fails naming the finding id, `authors_say` with 'UNRESOLVED' fails naming the card id, and 'UNRESOLVED'/'Not Examined' inside a claim `sources[].quote` and a card `sources[].quote` pass. (e) `a_second_study_directory_is_checked_too` with a temp studies root. (f) a `degradation_warning` test over four inputs. (g) ports of the quote, SHA and range mutation checks from the old firstmate test, using ids read from the data instead of the literals c1 and ra1.

lib.rs: add `fn study_dir_of(path) -> Option<&str>` (a `studies/<id>/<rest>` path whose segments are all plain, with a non-empty id and rest) and extend `admit()`. Build-output paths produce `build-output` as before and are skipped by the new checks. More than one id gives one `study-one-directory` violation naming the ids. Each other path that is not exactly `CHANGELOG.md` and not under a study directory gives a `study-outside-directory` violation with its path. Add tests for the six cases in the criterion 3 demonstration, keeping `build_output_is_refused` as is.

xtask/tests/policy.rs: split `boundary_scan` into `scan_words` and `scan_fragments`, keeping `boundary_scan` as their union so the admission-agreement test is unchanged. Add `claim_quote_exempt(path)` (exactly `studies/<one id>/claims.json`), `without_claim_quotes(text)` and `boundary_scan_file(path, text)`. `without_claim_quotes` parses the text with serde_json and collects every `sources[].quote` string of the claims. It then finds each `"quote"\s*:\s*"(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*"` match with a regex, decodes the literal with `serde_json::from_str::<String>`, and replaces the whole match with `"quote": ""` when the decoded value is in the collected set. One line stays one line. If parsing fails, nothing is blanked. `boundary_scan_file` matches words on the blanked text and fragments on the raw text. Use it in `athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where`. Add tests for each case in the criterion 4 demonstration, including the escaped-character quote, planting words and fragments with `.concat()` from split parts. Grep the file for the banned words before finishing.
crates/athena-cap-study/Cargo.toml: add `tempfile.workspace = true` under [dev-dependencies]. Cargo.lock: add "tempfile" after "serde_json" in the athena-cap-study entry.

producer.md: keep every existing rule and add the three conventions with at most about 72 bytes of net growth (the current file is 1019 bytes). Draft: tighten the opening line; merge the tag rule into the claim bullet (`start its text [mechanism] or [prose-only]`); change the model bullet to `A guard that does not exist is none, never checked by code`; add one line `No placeholders (UNRESOLVED, not examined) outside quotes. Quotes stay verbatim.`; add `Change one studies/<id>/ and CHANGELOG.md only.` only if the set stays within 1043. Do not write the scan's word list and avoid the text 'agent-reference'. Then run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets` and `cargo test -p athena-context`. If `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` or `every_role_set_is_within_its_budget` fails because the study set passed the recorded 1043, shorten the prompt: drop the one-directory line first, then trim wording. Never edit docs/system-facts.md or any budget.

CHANGELOG.md: add the entry under [Unreleased] / ### Changed, without the banned words. It covers per-study validation, the prompt conventions (quotes are exempt from the placeholder check), the admission refusal, the boundary exemption for claim quotes, the pinning precondition (ATHENA_PIN_* must be set by the pinning change) and the degradation (conventions only, with a warning, when it is unset, so the verifier prompt's claim holds only after that change), and the note that a study sharing a repository URL with another fails the kept test when its pin has the same URL and a different SHA than ATHENA_PIN_*.

Run `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --locked` (or the crate tests named in the demonstrations: `cargo test -p athena-cap-study`, `cargo test -p xtask --test policy`, `cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets`, `cargo test -p athena-context`, `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus`). Where pinned-source/ and ATHENA_PIN_* are present, confirm the log shows firstmate fully validated. Run `git status` and confirm nothing under studies/, no athena.toml and no docs/system-facts.md changed.

risks.risk: The ATHENA_PIN_* variables may not reach the test process, so tree validation would silently not run. That is weaker than today's behavior of validating whenever pinned-source/ exists.
risks.mitigation: The kept test prints, per study, 'fully validated' or 'conventions only'. When pinned-source/ is a directory and no study matched, it prints the greppable line 'WARNING: mounted tree present but no study matched ATHENA_PIN_*; tree validation did not run'. `degradation_warning` is unit-tested. The CHANGELOG names the pinning precondition and the degradation. The rebuilt-tree tests run the full-validation route in every checkout.

risks.risk: The reconstructed tree is built from the study's own citations, so it cannot show that the real tree holds the quotes.
risks.mitigation: The test's doc comment says so. The matching-pin cases assert the route and that a tampered validation.json or a changed quote is caught. Only a mounted tree proves the quotes; criterion 1's mounted command covers that on a host with pinned-source/.

risks.risk: Several single-line ranges in firstmate's claims.json are shared by different quotes, so a one-quote-per-line tree collides. A quote containing a newline could shift later lines.
risks.mitigation: `synthetic_tree` joins quotes that start on one line with a space and pads to the highest end line. The tests assert `bad_citation` and `quote_mismatch` are empty on the tree before comparing, so a placement fault is reported by claim id. Before writing, the producer greps firstmate's claims.json for escaped newlines in quotes and for non-file source kinds, and reports what it finds.

risks.risk: The prompt must carry three conventions and exemption wording in about 72 bytes of net growth, and may not fit.
risks.mitigation: The producer tightens existing sentences (merges the tag rule into the claim bullet, shortens the opening line) and runs the budgets test. If the set is still over 1043, the one-directory sentence goes first, because admission enforces it and its violation names the allowed set. Wording is cut before any of the three conventions. docs/system-facts.md is never edited and the budget is never raised.

risks.risk: A parsed-value walk could miss placeholder text in a field shape it does not expect, or flag a key name.
risks.mitigation: The walk checks every string value in every study file and no keys. Tests cover claim text, finding detail, card `authors_say` and the quote exemption in both claims and cards.

risks.risk: A regex over raw claims.json could blank a `quote` literal that is not a source quote.
risks.mitigation: A literal is blanked only when its decoded string equals a `sources[].quote` of the parsed claims. A same-valued string elsewhere under a `quote` key is a copy of a claim quote anyway. Everything else, and a file that does not parse, stays scanned.

risks.risk: Study jobs that legitimately touch another path (for example a shared doc) are now refused.
risks.mitigation: The brief expects about 5% newly refused readings. The violation detail names the allowed set (one studies/<id>/ plus CHANGELOG.md) so the producer can fix the change in one retry.

risks.risk: A studied system's words in a rationale-card quote, `authors_say`, or a claim's own prose still fail the boundary scan.
risks.mitigation: The request exempts only claim quotes. Raised as a User question.

risks.risk: With several studies of one repository, the same-URL-different-SHA failure can fire for a study the job did not pick.
risks.mitigation: The request's rule is kept. The failure names the study id and both SHAs, the CHANGELOG records the conflict, and the third open question asks whether to relax it.

demonstrations.method: Run the study crate tests. The kept test `every_study_follows_the_conventions_and_the_matching_one_validates` calls `check_studies(studies root, env pair read from ATHENA_PIN_URL/ATHENA_PIN_SHA, mount ../../pinned-source if it is a directory)` and prints one line per study: `<id>: fully validated` or `<id>: conventions only`. `the_study_matching_the_pin_validates_against_a_tree_rebuilt_from_its_citations` passes the study's own URL and SHA as the env pair and a `synthetic_tree` as the mount. It asserts `bad_citation` and `quote_mismatch` are empty on that tree, then route == FullyValidated, no problems, and computed validation equal to validation.json. `a_matching_pin_runs_validation_and_reports_a_tampered_record_or_quote` copies the study to a TempDir and calls `check_study` with the pin's own URL and SHA and a tree built from the untouched study. Case (i) flips one rule result in the copy's validation.json. Case (ii) changes one claim quote. Case (iii) makes the same quote change with the env pair unset. `a_second_study_directory_is_checked_too` builds a temp studies root with the firstmate copy and a renamed copy holding an untagged claim. Mounted-case command for a host with pinned-source/: `ATHENA_PIN_URL=<repository_url in studies/firstmate-work-handling/pin.json> ATHENA_PIN_SHA=<sha in the same file> cargo test -p athena-cap-study rules::tests -- --nocapture`.
demonstrations.observes: With no ATHENA_PIN_* set, every studies/*/ passes the conventions and the output says 'conventions only'. The rebuilt-tree test passes with route FullyValidated. Case (i) returns route FullyValidated and a problem containing the study id and 'validation.json'. Case (ii) returns a problem containing the claim id and 'quote-mismatch'. Case (iii) returns ConventionsOnly and no problems. The second-directory test fails naming the second directory and its claim id. In the mounted case (host only) the printed line says 'firstmate-work-handling: fully validated'. This job's verifier has no pinned-source/ and cannot see that case.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the matching branch returned early without calling `validate()`, cases (i) and (ii) would return no problems and the route assertion would fail. If the loop skipped a directory, the second-directory test would not name the bad claim. If `synthetic_tree` collided on shared single-line ranges, the pre-check would name the claim and fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `validate()` and the 18 rules exist in rules.rs. New test-module items `check_study` (returning `Outcome`), `check_studies`, `Loaded::read(dir)`, `NoTree`, `synthetic_tree(&Loaded) -> TempDir` and the copy helper are added by plan steps 1-4. `MountedTree` exists (rules.rs:1412) and is generalised in step 1. Fixtures are the real studies/ directory and `tempfile::TempDir` copies. Root, env pair and mount are injected as arguments. The doubles hold no rule logic.

demonstrations.method: The test copies the first study directory into a TempDir, edits its JSON with serde_json, then calls `check_study`. (a) Set claims[0].text to untagged prose: a problem containing that claim id and 'enforcement'. (b) Set transitions[0].guard to "none" and guard_evaluated_by to "code": a problem naming the transition id. (c) Set claims[0].sources[0].sha to a different 40-hex SHA: a problem naming the claim id (via `wrong_sha`). (d) Leave the copy unchanged and pass an env pair with the pin's URL and a different SHA, with a temp dir as mount: a problem naming the study id and both SHAs. A control (unmodified copy, env unset) returns no problems. A second test, `the_word_unresolved_in_prose_is_not_a_placeholder` (run with `cargo test -p athena-cap-study rules::tests::the_word_unresolved_in_prose_is_not_a_placeholder`), covers finding 2: a claim text 'conflicts are left unresolved' passes; the placeholder 'UNRESOLVED' in claim text fails naming the claim id; 'Not Examined' in a finding detail fails naming the finding id; 'UNRESOLVED' in a rationale `authors_say` fails naming the card id; 'UNRESOLVED' and 'Not Examined' inside a claim's `sources[].quote` and a card's `sources[].quote` pass.
demonstrations.observes: Four asserts of the form `problems.iter().any(|p| p.contains(<id>))` plus the control returning empty. Failure strings begin with the offending id. The lowercase 'unresolved' passes, the placeholder in prose fails, and the same words inside a source quote pass.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the tag check, the none-guard check, the SHA check or the pin-mismatch check were removed, the matching case would return an empty list and its assertion would fail. If a message omitted the id, `contains(id)` would fail. A case-insensitive UNRESOLVED check would fail the 'left unresolved' test. A raw-text scan would fail the quote-exempt cases.
demonstrations.seam: `check_study(dir, pin_env, mount)` is added in step 3 and the placeholder walk in step 2. Fixtures are `tempfile::TempDir` copies of the real study, with `tempfile` added to dev-dependencies in step 7. The pin env pair and mount are injected as arguments. The conventions run the real `wrong_sha` rule with a `NoTree` lookup (added in step 1) that only supplies absent git answers.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in lib.rs call `Study.admit(&ChangeList, &job_config())`. Input forms and cases: (1) studies/a/claims.json, studies/a/model.json and CHANGELOG.md give none. (2) studies/a/claims.json and studies/b/claims.json give one `study-one-directory` violation naming a and b. (3) studies/a/claims.json and docs/x.md give one `study-outside-directory` violation with path docs/x.md. (4) CHANGELOG.md alone gives none. (5) docs/CHANGELOG.md, bare studies/x, studies/a/../b/c, and a deleted file under a second directory are refused. (6) target/debug/x with studies/s1/claims.json gives exactly one violation, the existing build-output case. athena-core's refusal_corpus covers request-reading checks. A grep of crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs for admit, ChangeList and studies/ found no case for change-path admission, so no corpus case maps to these forms and none is added. This is a change-path admission rule, not a request-reading rule. `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` can still be run to show the reading corpus is unchanged; no result is cited here.
demonstrations.observes: Violations returned by `admit()` equal the expected rule names and paths for every case. The existing `build_output_is_refused` still passes. The tightening is intended: expected 5% of study readings newly refused.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the old admit, the two-directory and outside-file cases return zero violations, so the count and rule-name assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: `Study::admit` exists (crates/athena-cap-study/src/lib.rs:112). Callers reach it through the `Capability` trait at crates/athena-core/src/run/candidate.rs:164 and run/mod.rs:783. The seam is a directly built `ChangeList` and the existing `job_config()` fixture (lib.rs:132). The helper `study_dir_of(path) -> Option<&str>` is added in step 5 and is called by the real code, not faked.

demonstrations.method: New tests call the new `boundary_scan_file(path, text)` (step 6). Claims JSON is built with `serde_json::json!` and `to_string_pretty`, and one case is hand-written JSON with escaped characters. The planted word and machine-path fragment are built with `.concat()` from split parts, as in `the_boundary_scanner_flags_a_planted_term` (policy.rs:187). Cases: a banned word in a claim's source quote in studies/s/claims.json gives no hit. The same word in the claim's `text` gives a hit. The word in studies/s/findings.json or studies/s/notes.md gives a hit. The same claims JSON at docs/x/claims.json, crates/x/claims.json or studies/a/b/claims.json gives a hit. A machine-path fragment inside a claim quote gives a hit. A word in a rationale-card quote in studies/s/rationales.json gives a hit. A hand-written claim quote with `\/`, `\"` and `é` escapes around the planted word gives no hit. Invalid JSON in claims.json exempts nothing. `athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where` calls the new function over tracked files. A Grep of xtask/tests/policy.rs for each banned word in the list there (not written in this plan) must find no match outside the existing `boundary_words()` list itself.
demonstrations.observes: All new tests and the existing M19 tests pass: `the_boundary_scanner_flags_a_planted_term`, `the_producer_brief_lists_exactly_the_scanners_terms`, `the_admission_scan_finds_what_the_policy_scan_finds` and the tree scan.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the exemption were missing, the claim-quote case would report a hit. If the exemption covered all of claims.json, the claim-text case would report none. If fragments were also exempted, the fragment-in-quote case would report none. If matching used a re-serialized text instead of the decoded literal, the escaped-quote case would report a hit.

open_questions: Host: Are ATHENA_PIN_URL and ATHENA_PIN_SHA set in the environment of study jobs' producer, verifier and cargo checks? A search of this snapshot (*.rs, *.md, *.toml) finds no code that sets them, and athena.toml's [capabilities.study.env] (out of scope) lists only CARGO_TARGET_DIR and CARGO_TERM_COLOR. If unset, the kept test checks conventions only and prints the mounted-tree warning, and the verifier prompt's claim that code already ran the validation rules is false until the pinning change lands.

User: Should rationale-card source quotes and a card's `authors_say` be exempt from the boundary scan, and `authors_say` from the placeholder check, as well? The request names only the quote fields of a study's claims for the scan, so the plan exempts only claims.json source quotes there, and exempts only `sources[].quote` from the placeholder check. A studied system's own words in a card quote still fail the boundary scan.

User: Several studies may share one repository URL (pin.rs `study_pin` picks one by the study id in the request), but ATHENA_PIN_URL and ATHENA_PIN_SHA carry no study id. The request's rule makes every other study of that URL with a different SHA fail the kept test. The plan keeps the rule as asked; should it instead skip, not fail, a same-URL study whose SHA differs once the pinning change can pass the study id?
